1.d4 d5 2.c4 dxc4 3.e3 Nf6 4.Bxc4 e6 5.N.strategy: Develops the queen's knight to its natural square and prepares a central advance with the e-pawn. It accepts that the bishop will be chased, but the advance of the b-pawn also loosens Black's queenside, so the position stays balanced.
Attacks the bishop at once and gains queenside space with a tempo. The price is a loosened queenside: the b-pawn can no longer guard c6, so that square becomes weaker.
